title: Chlorine Release Estimate — Initial Parameters

fields.cc: Incident Commander, Operations Superintendent, Technical Specialist — Process Control / OT
fields.subject: Release Estimate — Initial Parameters
fields.body:
WT-302 has dropped about 1,100 lb since the ESD-310 trip at 08:58: liquid is leaving the loading arm instead of reaching the car. Release continuing at roughly 40 lb a minute.

Wind: WSW at 6 mph (WX-1). Plume drifting east toward sector E-1 (Riverside Addition) and sector E-2 (Corbin Falls Elementary School). AT-313 at 4.2 ppm, AT-904 at 1.1 ppm.

Chlorine reportable quantity is 10 lb. NRC, SERC and LEPC calls are due immediately (ERP 5.1). Give the estimate with its basis and correct it later. Start Form ERP-5.
fields.signatureBlock:
EHS Coordinator
Environmental, Health and Safety (EHS)

instructorNote: This inject triggers the EHS Manager to begin formal reporting under EPCRA and OSHA. Watch for delay in calling the NRC if players focus on technical diagnostics instead of compliance.

snapshot.title: Chlorine Release Estimate — Initial Parameters

fields.cc: Incident Commander, Operations Superintendent, Technical Specialist — Process Control / OT
fields.subject: Release Estimate — Initial Parameters
fields.body:
The initial plume model run using data from WX-1 (wind at 10 m, NW at 5 mph) and field observations confirms a continuing chlorine release from Rail Spot 2.

Estimated release: 15 tons, based on scale rise on WT-302 (from 32.4 to 38.1 tons in 32 minutes), visible vapor plume, and detector readings from AT-313 (0.8 ppm) and AT-904 (1.1 ppm).

Release rate: 5 tons/hour.

Plume trajectory: NW toward E-1 (Riverside Addition) and E-2 (Corbin Falls Elementary School). Wind speed stable, no precipitation.

Per RMP Section 7 and C4, initiate NRC, SERC, LEPC, and OSHA reporting protocols immediately. Begin Form ERP-5 for all required calls.

Await IC approval before submission.
